questions.stem: In some state of matter the molecules are oscillating near their points of equilibrium and cannot move freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?

options.A: A gas
options.B: A solid
options.C: A liquid
options.D: A fluid

explanation_steps: In a solid, molecules vibrate about fixed equilibrium positions and cannot move freely.
Gases and vapours move freely; liquids can flow. A fluid means liquid or gas. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the linear motion of an object with constant velocity?

questions.stem: A body starts from rest and acquires a velocity of 10 m/s in 5 s. What are the acceleration of the body and the distance traveled by it during this time interval?

options.A: 4 m/s², 20 m
options.B: 2 m/s², 25 m
options.C: 2 m/s², 40 m
options.D: 2 m/s², 20 m
options.E: 2 m/s², 10 m

explanation_steps: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½×2×25 = 25 m. Use g only where needed; here motion is given by the speed change. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: A body starts from rest and acquires a velocity of $$ 15m/s $$ in $$ 25m $$ what are the acceleration of the body and the time taken?

options.B: ... (rest of options from OCR)
options.E: none

explanation_steps:
**Given:**
Initial velocity $$ u = 0 $$
Final velocity $$ v = 15m/s $$
Distance $$ s = 25m $$

**Step 1: Find Acceleration ($$ a $$)**
Using $$ v^2 = u^2 + 2as $$
$$ 15^2 = 0^2 + 2 \times a \times 25 $$
$$ 225 = 50a $$
$$ a = 4.5 m/s^2 $$

**Step 2: Find Time ($$ t $$)**
Using $$ v = u + at $$
$$ 15 = 0 + 4.5 \times t $$
$$ t = \frac{15}{4.5} = 3.33 s $$

Since no option matches $$ a = 4.5 m/s^2 $$ and $$ t = 3.33 s $$, the answer is None.

similar_questions.stem: An object starts from rest and its velocity becomes 20m/s in 5s. The distance travelled by it during this time interval, in metres, is
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
Initial velocity ($$ u $$) = 0 m/s
Final velocity ($$ v $$) = 20 m/s
Time ($$ t $$) = 5 s

**Formula:**
For uniform acceleration, distance ($$ s $$) is:
$$ s = \frac{u + v}{2} \times t $$

**Calculation:**
$$ s = \frac{0 + 20}{2} \times 5 $$
$$ s = 10 \times 5 = 50 \text{ m} $$

**Result:** 50 metres.

similar_questions.stem: A 1 kg mass of cotton, a 2 kg mass of feather and a 3 kg mass of iron are released from a tower of 20 m height at the same time. Neglecting air resistance which one will hit the ground first?

options.A: Cotton
options.B: Feather
options.C: Iron
options.D: Cotton and feather
options.E: All hit at the same time.

explanation_steps: Without air resistance every body falls with the same acceleration g, independent of its mass (G9 p.92).
All start from rest at the same height, so h = ½gt² gives the same time for all: t = √(2h/g) = √(2 × 20/10) = 2 s. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?

options.B: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.
options.C: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is directed toward the center of the circle.
options.D: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is perpendicular to its acceleration.
options.E: The acceleration of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.

explanation_steps: Velocity in uniform circular motion is tangential, not toward the centre. The centripetal acceleration points to the centre.
A, B, D and E are true. The incorrect statement is C.

A race car starting from rest accelerates at constant acceleration of $$ 5m/s^2 $$. The velocity of the car after it has travelled 40m in m/s is:

options.E: None

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
- Initial velocity ($$ u $$) = 0
- Acceleration ($$ a $$) = $$ 5m/s^2 $$
- Distance ($$ s $$) = $$ 40m $$

**Step 2: Use the kinematic equation.**
$$ v^2 = u^2 + 2as $$

**Step 3: Solve for $$ v $$.**
$$ v^2 = 0^2 + 2(5)(40) = 400 $$
$$ v = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ m/s} $$.

similar_questions.stem: A truck is travelling at a speed of 65 km/h in the west direction along a straight road and a bus is traveling directly towards the truck at a speed of 45 km/h in the same road in east direction. The velocity of the truck with respect to the bus when they cross each other, is

options.A: 110 km/h towards west.
options.B: 110 km/h towards east.
options.C: 20 km/h towards west.
options.D: 20 km/h towards east.
options.E: 55 km/h towards west.

explanation_steps: Relative velocity: v(truck relative to bus) = v(truck) − v(bus) (G10 p.19–23).
Take west as positive: v(truck) = +65 km/h, v(bus) = −45 km/h (east).
v(truck rel. bus) = 65 − (−45) = +110 km/h, i.e. 110 km/h towards the west. Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: An object was initially at a distance of 10 cm in front of a plane mirror. If the object starts to move at a constant speed of 5 cm/s away from the reflecting surface of the mirror, after a time interval of 25 seconds the image and the object may be separated by
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate the distance moved by the object: $$ \text{dist} = \text{speed} \times \text{time} = 5 \text{ cm/s} \times 25 \text{ s} = 125 \text{ cm} $$.
**Step 2:** Find the final distance of the object from the mirror: $$ d_{object} = 10 \text{ cm} (\text{initial}) + 125 \text{ cm} = 135 \text{ cm} $$.
**Step 3:** In a plane mirror, the image distance equals the object distance ($$ d_{image} = 135 \text{ cm} $$).
**Step 4:** The separation between the object and its image is $$ d_{object} + d_{image} = 135 + 135 = 270 \text{ cm} $$.

questions.stem: If a ray of light goes obliquely from water to air, then the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence is

options.A: Larger than the angle of incidence.
options.B: Always less than the angle of incidence.
options.C: Equal to the angle of incidence.
options.D: Not related to the angle of incidence.
options.E: Less or equal to the angle of incidence.

explanation_steps: Water has a higher refractive index than air, so an oblique ray bends away from the normal.
Therefore the angle of refraction is larger than the angle of incidence (until the critical angle). Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: When a ray of light passes from optically rarer medium to optically denser medium at an angle of incidence different from $$ 0^\circ $$,

options.B: its angle of refraction becomes less than its angle of incidence.
options.C: its speed in the second medium is greater than in the first medium.
options.D: it bends away from the normal line.
options.E: total internal reflection takes place.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Refraction Rules.**
- **Rarer to Denser:** Light slows down and bends **towards** the normal. This makes the angle of refraction ($$ r $$) smaller than the angle of incidence ($$ i $$).
- **Denser to Rarer:** Light speeds up and bends away from the normal.

questions.stem: A spherical convex mirror with an object placed at a distance equal to the radius of curvature (R) from the surface of the mirror produces

options.A: A virtual image behind the mirror at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
options.B: A virtual, diminished image behind the mirror at a distance less than the radius of curvature.

Since the charges have opposite signs (one positive, one negative), the force is **attractive**.
